Class EMFModelGenerator

java.lang.Object
io.github.lorenzobettini.emfmodelgenerator.EMFModelGenerator
public class EMFModelGenerator extends Object
Main entry point for programmatically generating EMF model instances.

This class provides methods to generate model instances from Ecore metamodels, with support for automatic attribute population, reference handling, and XMI serialization.

Basic Usage: 

EMFModelGenerator generator = new EMFModelGenerator();
EPackage ePackage = generator.loadEcoreModel("model.ecore");
EClass personClass = (EClass) ePackage.getEClassifier("Person");

generator.setOutputDirectory("output/");
EObject person = generator.generateFrom(personClass);
generator.save();

generator.unloadEcoreModels(); // Clean up

Loading Ecore Models: Use loadEcoreModel(String) to load the first package from an Ecore file, or loadEcoreModelPackages(String) to access every top-level and nested package. These methods automatically register the resource factory and package registry entries. Call unloadEcoreModels() when done to clean up resources and registry entries.

Generation Methods:

  • generateFrom(EClass) - Generate a single instance from an EClass
  • generateFrom(EPackage) - Generate from the first instantiable EClass in a package
  • generateFromSeveral(EClass...) - Generate instances from multiple EClasses
  • generateAllFrom(EPackage) - Generate instances of all EClasses in a package
  • generateAllFrom(EClass) - Generate instances of all subclasses of an EClass

Customization: For population-related customization (custom setters, per-feature functions, multiplicities, depth, cycle policies, etc.), obtain the EMFInstancePopulator via getInstancePopulator() and configure it directly.

Post-generation validation: Generation fills features where suitable values are available. In particular, a required non-containment reference can remain unset when the generated population has no assignable target. Use validate() to inspect and handle the validation result: 

generator.generateFrom(personClass);
EMFValidationResult result = generator.validate();
if (!result.isValid()) {
    result.rejectedDiagnostics().forEach(diagnostic ->
        System.err.println(diagnostic.getMessage()));
}
Alternatively, use validateOrThrow() when an invalid candidate should stop the workflow: 
generator.generateFrom(personClass);
generator.validateOrThrow();
Validation before saving is optional and disabled by default. Enabling it prevents any resource from being serialized when validation fails: 
generator.enableValidationBeforeSave();
generator.save();
To validate the serialized form instead, save and reload the generated resources in a fresh resource set: 
EMFValidationResult roundTripResult = generator.saveAndValidateRoundTrip();
EMFValidationResult customRoundTripResult = generator.saveAndValidateRoundTrip(
    options, resourceSet -> new MyProjectModelValidator(resourceSet));
A custom implementation can be supplied through EMFModelValidator.Factory: 
EMFModelValidator.Factory factory = resourceSet ->
    new MyProjectModelValidator(resourceSet);
EMFValidationResult customResult = generator.validate(factory);
generator.enableValidationBeforeSave(factory);

Lorenzo Bettini

  • Constructor Details

    • EMFModelGenerator

      public EMFModelGenerator()
      Create a new EMFModelGenerator with default settings. A new ResourceSet will be created and reused for all generation calls.

    • EMFModelGenerator

      public EMFModelGenerator(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.resource.ResourceSet resourceSet)
      Create a new EMFModelGenerator with an external ResourceSet. The provided ResourceSet will be reused across multiple generation calls, and state (generated instances, counters) will be preserved between calls.

      Note: When using this constructor, you may still use loadEcoreModel(String) or loadEcoreModelPackages(String), which automatically register the EcoreResourceFactoryImpl if needed.

      Example usage: 

      ResourceSet resourceSet = new ResourceSetImpl();
resourceSet.getResourceFactoryRegistry().getExtensionToFactoryMap()
    .put("xmi", new XMIResourceFactoryImpl());

EMFModelGenerator generator = new EMFModelGenerator(resourceSet);
EPackage ePackage = generator.loadEcoreModel("model.ecore");
EClass personClass = (EClass) ePackage.getEClassifier("Person");

generator.setOutputDirectory("output");

// First generation
EObject person1 = generator.generateFrom(personClass);

// Second generation - reuses same ResourceSet and can reference
// instances from first generation
EObject person2 = generator.generateFrom(personClass);

// All resources are in the same ResourceSet
generator.save(); // Saves all generated resources

generator.unloadEcoreModels(); // Clean up
      Parameters:
      resourceSet - the ResourceSet to use for all generations

    • getInstancePopulator

      public final EMFInstancePopulator getInstancePopulator()
      Get the EMFInstancePopulator used to populate generated instances. Use this to configure population behavior such as custom setters, functions, multiplicities, depth limits, and cycle policies.

      Example: 

      generator.getInstancePopulator().setMaxDepth(3);
generator.getInstancePopulator().setContainmentReferenceDefaultMaxCount(4);
generator.getInstancePopulator().setAttributeSetter(myCustomSetter);
      Returns:
      the instance populator

    • loadEcoreModel

      public org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EPackage loadEcoreModel(String ecoreFilePath) throws IOException
      Load the first package from an Ecore model at the given file path. This method:
      • Registers the EcoreResourceFactoryImpl if not already registered
      • Loads the Ecore file into the shared ResourceSet
      • Registers all discovered EPackages in the shared and global registries
      • Tracks the loaded resource and owned registrations for cleanup via unloadEcoreModels()

      The first package in resource and depth-first subpackage traversal order is returned. Use loadEcoreModelPackages(String) when access to all packages is required.

      Example usage: 

      EMFModelGenerator generator = new EMFModelGenerator();
EPackage myPackage = generator.loadEcoreModel("models/mymodel.ecore");
EClass myClass = (EClass) myPackage.getEClassifier("MyClass");
EObject instance = generator.generateFrom(myClass);
generator.save();
generator.unloadEcoreModels(); // Clean up
      Parameters:
      ecoreFilePath - the path to the Ecore file (absolute or relative)
      Returns:
      the first loaded EPackage
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file cannot be loaded or has no top-level EPackage

    • loadEcoreModelPackages

      public List<org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EPackage> loadEcoreModelPackages(String ecoreFilePath) throws IOException
      Load all packages contained in one Ecore resource.

      Top-level packages are inspected in resource order. Each package is followed by its subpackages recursively in their natural order. Every package with a nonblank namespace URI is registered without replacing existing entries in either the shared ResourceSet registry or the global registry. The returned list is immutable.

      Parameters:
      ecoreFilePath - the path to the Ecore file (absolute or relative)
      Returns:
      all loaded top-level and nested EPackages in deterministic traversal order
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file cannot be loaded or has no top-level EPackage

    • unloadEcoreModels

      public void unloadEcoreModels()
      Unload all Ecore models loaded via loadEcoreModel(String) or loadEcoreModelPackages(String). This method:
      • Unloads the Ecore resources from the shared ResourceSet
      • Removes only package registrations inserted by this generator
      • Clears the tracking lists

      This method is safe to call multiple times. It only affects Ecore models loaded through these loading methods, not other packages or resources.

    • validate

      public EMFValidationResult validate()
      Performs post-generation validation of all model roots using standard EMF validation.

      This method validates the current in-memory objects. It does not save or reload them. Use saveAndValidateRoundTrip() to validate the serialized form.

      Validation covers every root in every non-Ecore resource in this generator's resource set. When an external ResourceSet was supplied, this includes its existing non-Ecore resources, matching the scope of save().

      Returns:
      the aggregate validation result

    • validate

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      the aggregate validation result
      Throws:

      public void save() throws IOException
      Save all generated models to XMI files. The file names are determined by the resources created during generation. Ecore files are automatically skipped.
      Throws:
      IOException - if the files cannot be written
      EMFValidationException - if validation before saving is enabled and the generated model fails validation

    • save

      public void save(Map<Object,Object> options) throws IOException
      Save all generated models to XMI files with custom options. The file names are determined by the resources created during generation. Ecore files are automatically skipped.

      Example usage with schemaLocation: 

      Map<Object, Object> options = new HashMap<>();
options.put(XMLResource.OPTION_SCHEMA_LOCATION, Boolean.TRUE);
generator.save(options);
      Parameters:
      options - the save options to pass to EMF resources, or null for default options
      Throws:
      IOException - if the files cannot be written
      EMFValidationException - if validation before saving is enabled and the generated model fails validation

    • saveAndValidateRoundTrip

      public EMFValidationResult saveAndValidateRoundTrip() throws IOException
      Saves all generated models, reloads exactly the saved resources in a fresh resource set, and validates every reloaded root using standard EMF validation.

      All resources are created and loaded together before references are resolved and validation begins, so references between saved resources can resolve. The returned result describes only the reconstructed objects, not the current in-memory objects. Temporary reload resources are unloaded and are never added to this generator's resource set.

      If validation before saving is enabled, it runs first with its configured validator and can prevent serialization in the same way as save(). Round-trip validation happens after a successful save; an invalid result does not remove files already written.

      Returns:
      the aggregate standard-validation result for the reloaded roots
      Throws:
      IOException - if the files cannot be written or reloaded
      EMFValidationException - if validation before saving is enabled and the current model fails validation

    • saveAndValidateRoundTrip

      public EMFValidationResult saveAndValidateRoundTrip(Map<Object,Object> options, EMFModelValidator.Factory validatorFactory) throws IOException
      Saves all generated models with custom options, reloads exactly the saved resources in a fresh resource set, and validates every reloaded root using a validator created by the supplied factory.

      The save options are forwarded unchanged to the normal save path. All saved resources are loaded together before references are resolved and validation begins. The returned result describes only the reconstructed objects. Temporary reload resources are unloaded and are never added to this generator's resource set.

      The factory receives the fresh resource set containing the reloaded resources, not this generator's resource set. If validation before saving is enabled, its separately configured factory validates the current in-memory graph before serialization. The supplied factory applies only after a successful save to the reconstructed graph; an invalid round-trip result does not remove files already written.

      Parameters:
      options - the save options to pass to EMF resources, or null for default options
      validatorFactory - the factory used to create one validator for the fresh round-trip resource set
      Returns:
      the supplied validator's result for the reconstructed model only
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the factory, validator, or result is null; a null factory is rejected before any save-related filesystem side effect
      IOException - if the files cannot be written or reloaded
      EMFValidationException - if validation before saving is enabled and the current model fails validation
